subject: Linguistics
title: Language and Nationalism
description: A short lesson to help you apply Language and Nationalism.

hook.text: When Croatia split from Yugoslavia, Croatian and Serbian were declared separate languages—overnight.

buildup.text: National languages are often political constructs as much as linguistic ones.

discovery.text: A 'language' is sometimes just 'a dialect with an army and a navy,' as the saying goes.

twist.text: Hindi and Urdu are mutually intelligible but treated as different languages for political reasons.

climax.text: Language standardization is a tool of nation-building—one nation, one language is the ideology.

punchline.text: A language is a dialect with political power.

quiz.question: What determines whether a variety is a 'language' or a 'dialect'?
